title: Seams & Tangles Review (periodical run 11): round 1 of LIN-4344 as the coherence baseline, window 7–9 Nov in both repos (LinearViewer delta vs run 10 at b315e0e8f; simple-dispatcher first baseline at 5d8489e)
description:
## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="seams-tangles" -->
"Read the window 7 Nov 00:00 UTC to 9 Nov 00:00 UTC (round 1 of "Harbour carries the loop", LIN-4344; main up to b315e0e8f) in both repos. This reading is the coherence baseline for the work that follows, so read only that window."

**The line above is the operator note, carried word for word.** It says why this run exists: round 1 of LIN-4344 has landed, and this reading is the baseline the work after it will be measured against. It is context, not scope. In practice it fixes three things: the end commit (`b315e0e8f` in LinearViewer, `5d8489e` in simple-dispatcher; do not move HEAD forward if main has moved since), the window (7 Nov 00:00 to 9 Nov 00:00 UTC), and that **both repositories** are read.

Repositories: `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour) and `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher`, branch `main` in both. Minted against LinearViewer `b315e0e8f3e1e5f3b5d6e634e53c5dc83b41d754` and simple-dispatcher `5d8489e7fd8434f0e69af7df11a3746790abbe64`. Check everything below against those commits when you start. The figures here are a starting point, not findings.

## What this is

Seams & Tangles periodical, **run 11**: the direction and tangling *between areas* (knots, wrong-way dependencies, hubs, ways in, rebuild readiness, where the guide's names differ from the graph, change coupling). It is framed as a delta against run 10 for LinearViewer, and as a **first baseline** for simple-dispatcher. Review-only: the deliverable is a report plus area-note entries, merged through docs-only PRs, and then this task concluded.

## Starting scope (audit it and widen it before you execute)

Treat this as a floor. Before running the review, look for surfaces in this remit that are not listed here and fold them in. If you could only shrink this scope, be suspicious of that. Widen *what you examine*, never *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked, and a near-empty result is a genuine outcome. The area notes get an entry only where a finding binds a builder or waits in an area, and each note stays under its cap.

**Previous run (read it first).** `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-08-run10.md` (LIN-4387, PR #2372, merged `82fdb88be`), with evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-08-run10/`. It measured `bad9d719ba01ffea2ba5339c32ea354e67bf5682` against run 9's `90542b2c`, and checked that the edge dump at `e03a9a6ac` was the same. Its §10 trend ledger is the list you compare against: `seam:runner-contract` (two repos, Medium, new); F1 `knot:agents-chat<->runs` High (31/49); F6 `knot:browser-window-globals` Medium; N1 `knot:other-features-catch-all` Medium (18); `knot:agent-api<->other-features` Medium (new, opened by `lib/as-asked-seal.js`); N3 `knot:auth->llm(model-routing)` Low–Medium (6/4); the hubs `openrouter.js`, `workspace-preferences.js`, `dispatch-factory.js`, `periodicals.js`, `cost-read.js`, `dispatch-store.js`, `task-page-loader.js`, `run-controls.js`, `tree.js`; `wiring: server.js`; F3, F4, F5, F7, F8; `door:as-asked`; `guide hygiene: wake-credential`. Runs 1–9 sit beside it in `docs/reviews/`. Keep the stable names, and retire or add names explicitly.

**The window, in LinearViewer.** The operator's window starts at `aec9e16be` (the last main commit before 7 Nov 00:00 UTC) and ends at `b315e0e8f`: 39 first-parent commits, 103 production files changed (+5806 / −1597). Run 10 already measured most of it, up to `bad9d719`. **Compare against run 10's measured commit** `bad9d719`**, as the contract requires.** Then also give the whole-window figures from `aec9e16be`, because the operator asked for this window as the baseline. Since run 10 (`bad9d719..b315e0e8f`) there are 13 commits and 38 production files (+1025 / −471), with two new files: `lib/recommendation-look-first.js` and `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`. The themes since run 10 (from merge titles) are: the look-first route (LIN-4370), Periodicals feeding the notes (LIN-4380), landed lane state (LIN-4381), the autopilot precedence leaf (LIN-4382), removing the size-of-the-move setting (LIN-4393, which touches `workspace-preferences.js`, `settings-areas.js` and `routes/settings.js`), the area-notes pointer (LIN-4346), the review tail driving the review in place (LIN-4349), and LIN-4358's after-reads. Some leads to check (these are not conclusions):

* Where does `lib/recommendation-look-first.js` land in the registry, and does it open a new Recommendation/Runs ↔ notes edge?
* LIN-4393 may have shrunk `hub:workspace-preferences.js`.
* `routes/proxy-compute.js` grew.
* Run 10's adversarial reader could not read simple-dispatcher's side of the runner contract.

**The window, in simple-dispatcher: there is no prior Seams run there.** Window `07c88f7..5d8489e`: 7 first-parent commits, 20 files (+1875 / −116). They are: area notes arriving (LIN-4372), the session's own PR in `[done]` (LIN-4375), the broker 429 back-off and the contract re-copy (LIN-4378, LIN-4385, `harbour-token-mcp-server.js`, `test/fixtures/runner-contract.json`), and the after-reads. Write this side as the **baseline** and compare nothing. **The measuring tool cannot read this repo as it stands.** `scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs` scopes only `server.js`, `lib/`, `routes/` and `public/`, and reads `import` statements. simple-dispatcher is root-level CommonJS (`require`). At `5d8489e`, with simple-dispatcher's own `docs/areas/areas.json`, it returns 0 areas and 0 links. Report that as a could-not-read count, plainly, and do not edit the tool (this is review-only). Read simple-dispatcher's area seams through its own guide-side surfaces instead: `docs/module-map.md` (seam order) and `test/module-map-census.test.js`. `scripts/code-shape/cochange.mjs` does work on it (git history only): at mint, `--days 60` with simple-dispatcher's registry gave 104 changes, 50 multi-area, 15 pairs, 243 unmapped. Name the cross-repo seams the import graph cannot show: the runner contract (pinned by sha256 in both repos), the broker/limiter 429 policy, and the `[done]`/leftover wording Harbour renders into simple-dispatcher tasks.

**The guide and the tool.** The LinearViewer registry is `docs/areas/areas.json`. Run `bad9d719`, `aec9e16be` and HEAD with **the one HEAD registry**, so any difference is code that moved. If the registry was edited between those commits (check `git log` on it), also re-run the older commits with their own registry, and record what the guide edit alone moved, separately from code movement. Check whether `scripts/code-shape/` changed since `bad9d719`. If it did, confirm the HEAD tool reproduces run 10's `bad9d719` JSON before you trust any delta, and report any difference as a tool change. `scripts/code-shape/README.md` says how to run both tools.

**Change coupling.** Run `cochange.mjs --days 60` (the window length run 10 used) at `bad9d719` and at HEAD, with the same HEAD registry. Run 10's totals were 929 / 413 / 76, and its top pairs and its 19 pairs with no import link are in its §6 and §10. Report `unmappedFiles` and `shallow`. A pair that changes together often but has no import link between its areas is a candidate seam. This window's notes, leftover and look-first work spans several areas in single changes, so read the coupling in that light. This is about pairs of areas only. Per-file churn belongs to the Stability Review.

**Siblings: mind the altitude, do not double-flag.**

* Drift & Coherence owns decisions held in several places and the direction between individual files. Its latest report is `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-06.md`. Run 10 §11 handed it the `periodicals.js` content, and that hand-off was still open.
* Stability owns churn: `stability-review-2026-11-08.md` (LIN-4394, inside this window).
* Code Quality owns function size: find its latest report. None sits under that name in `docs/reviews/` at mint, so look for the convention.
* Comprehension Debt (`comprehension-debt-review-2026-11-05.md`) and Design & Interface (`design-interface-review-2026-11-08.md`, LIN-4391) have their own remits.

Cross-link them. A seam between two of their remits that none of them owns is still in this review's remit, and so is the seam between the two repositories.

**Known-issues surfaces to read.**

* Both repos' `CLAUDE.md`.
* LinearViewer's `docs/architecture/source-map.md` and `tests/unit/area-map-placement.test.js` (placements pinned because they were once wrong).
* Both repos' `docs/areas/README.md` and notes.
* Inline markers in the window's files.
* Open tickets. Owners at mint: LIN-3738 (Backlog, `proxy-preamble.js` out of Agent API, which is F4), LIN-3923 (Backlog, the LLM ⇄ Providers knot, which is F3), LIN-4318 (Backlog, periodical mint by id), LIN-4193 (Backlog, cost modules into an area), LIN-4028 (In Progress, routing ruling), LIN-4258/4259 (Backlog). Re-read their states. A finding already filed as a ticket stays in the report only.

## The review contract

 1. **Read prior runs first; this review is trend-aware.** Frame every LinearViewer knot as new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved against run 10, and report changes since run 10 first. For simple-dispatcher, say plainly that no prior run exists and that this is the baseline.
 2. **Run the measuring tools; do not re-derive the numbers by searching.** Record every full commit you measured. Report the tool's could-not-read counts rather than ignore them: parse failures, unresolved relative imports, non-literal dynamic imports, unmapped files, and simple-dispatcher's empty scope. Everything else is judgement, written as prose with no scores and no clustering: wrong-way dependencies (for example `lib/` → `routes/`, or run logic importing page renderers), hub modules, whether each area has a clear way in and whether callers use it, rebuild readiness per area and what stops it, and where the import graph's areas differ from the guide's names. These classes are a floor: find the complete set for this remit. Propose guide edits in the report, recorded apart from code movement, and add no test, check or count that enforces the guide.
 3. **Read change coupling beside import coupling**, as scoped above, with what moved since run 10. Report simple-dispatcher's pairs as its baseline.
 4. **Write an uncapped, severity-ranked report.** Ground each finding in the tool output at HEAD and the source it points to, not in earlier prose. Close with a compact trend ledger: each knot or area under a stable descriptive name, with its severity and its delta against run 10 (simple-dispatcher rows marked baseline). Record it where the convention puts it: `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-<date>-run11.md` in LinearViewer, with evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>-run11/` holding a `README.md`, as runs 1–10 did. simple-dispatcher has no report series, so its baseline lives in this same report. State plainly in the report that seams, and the cross-repo seam above all, have no full home in the notes yet.
 5. **Feed the area notes; mint no follow-up tasks.** Follow each repo's own `docs/areas/README.md` and Harbour's `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`, not this summary. That covers the registry `docs/areas/areas.json` (first match wins), one note per area at `docs/areas/<slug>.md` with `## Lessons` and `## Waiting`, the guard (`tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` in LinearViewer, `test/area-notes.test.js` in simple-dispatcher), and the 6144-byte cap per note.
    * Start from the files changed between the previous measured commit and HEAD (`bad9d719..b315e0e8f` in LinearViewer, `07c88f7..5d8489e` in simple-dispatcher). Map each to its area through that repo's registry, and look first where work landed.
    * In each note you touch, prune entries that are settled or no longer true, and distil it under the cap. At mint, `llm-and-prompts.md` is 6073 bytes and `runs-and-dispatch.md` is 6142, so either needs pruning before it can take anything.
    * A finding that leaves work in an area is a Waiting entry. A rule a builder there must follow is a Lesson.
    * Each entry cites the area's file first, names its source as "Seams & Tangles, <the date of this run>", and cites this report as the second path. In simple-dispatcher, a LinearViewer path is named in prose, not in backticks (its README's rule). So cite the report there as "Harbour's docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-<date>-run11.md".
    * An area with no note yet may get one only if a finding needs it, named exactly by its slug.
 6. **Route each finding with no area note to the person, never to a ticket.**
    * A larger tidy (a move bigger than a change should take on in passing) becomes a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, and is also listed for the person in the closing comment.
    * A finding with no file in an area to cite (a manifest or lockfile, or urgent breakage such as a live secret) goes in the closing comment only.
    * A cross-area seam is filed under the area a change would start from, naming the other side. A cross-repo seam is filed in the repo a change would start from.
    * If a repo has no area notes, every finding stays in the report and the closing comment only.
 7. **Docs-only pull requests, one per repository touched.** The LinearViewer PR holds the report, its evidence folder and LinearViewer's note edits. A simple-dispatcher PR exists only if its notes are edited, and holds only those edits. Branches follow each repo's convention (`feat/lin-<id>-…` or `chore/lin-<id>-…`). Rebase each onto `main`, get the required checks (LinearViewer's `ci-success`) and the notes guard green, and merge each yourself, since they are docs-only. Only if merging is genuinely impossible (no permission, or required checks still red) may you leave one open, and then only as an explicit handoff naming the blocker in the closing comment.
 8. **Fresh-context adversarial second-read: required before Done.** After the report and note edits are written, a separate reader answers cold: *"What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*
    * Tier 1 (preferred): a wholly separate session with no memory of this run.
    * Tier 2 (accepted): a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn. Give it read access to both clones.
    * Tier 3 (this session re-reading its own report) is not accepted.

    State which tier you used. Post one comment on this task carrying all three of these together in one body:
    * `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`;
    * `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict);
    * `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`.

    The engine refuses Done until all three are in one comment. Copy them into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude normally: DISAGREE is itself the escalation.
 9. **Then conclude; do not leave this task open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary as a comment here. Include the report's path, the merged PR(s), and, addressed to the person, any larger tidy and any finding with no area file to cite. Then move this task to Done.
10. **Stay review-only.** Change no code, config or secrets, and no docs beyond the report, its evidence folder and the area-note edits. That includes the measuring tools and both `docs/areas/areas.json` files: guide edits and tool gaps (such as the CommonJS blind spot) are proposals in the report.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the full two-repo Seams & Tangles reading as asked; no survey finding binds, since note pruning, the seam-home gap and the unreadable CommonJS scope are already inside the ask or are proposals it forbids building.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Research findings (10 Nov, at LinearViewer `b315e0e8f`, simple-dispatcher `5d8489e`)

Full notes, the per-layer audit and the classes are in the research comment. `origin/main` equals the mint commit in both repos, so nothing has moved since the ticket was created.

**Key findings**

* **LinearViewer: unchanged in structure since run 10.** The HEAD tools reproduce run 10's `bad9d719` seams and co-change JSON: seams differs only in `areaMapSource`, and co-change is identical. Neither the tool nor the registry changed after `bad9d719`. `aec9e16be` run with its own guide gives links identical to the run with the HEAD guide, so the guide edit alone moved nothing.
  * The knots are still 13 pairs and one 9-area group, with none new and none resolved.
  * LLM ⇄ Runs moved 31/49 → 32/50, Auth ⇄ LLM 6/4 → 5/3, Web → Auth 69 → 67, Agent API → Runs 45 → 44.
  * Exactly 4 crossings were added (three from `recommendation-look-first.js`, one `proxy-compute.js` → `run-evidence.js`) and 4 removed (two from LIN-4393 in workspace-preferences, two `routes/proxy.js` → Runs). The look-first file opens no edge to the notes.
  * Co-change moved 929/413/76 → 942/418/76. `unmappedFiles` went 7216 → 8061, and `shallow` is false. The 19 pairs with no import link are the same set.
* **simple-dispatcher: could-not-read.** `seams.mjs` scopes 0 of 52 root CommonJS files. Co-change is 104/50/15 with 243 unmapped; the top pair is Loop⇄State at 19.
  * **A spike confirmed a repeatable baseline:** a small require-graph reader using the same counting rules gives 52 files, 0 unmapped, 0 unresolved, 20 links and 6 reciprocal pairs.
  * Two of the six pairs come from one file, `shutdown.js`, which sits in State but requires Stop-hook and Reapers modules. That is a guide-placement finding, not a code tangle.
  * Loop⇄Test harnesses co-change 14 times with no require link. That is a process boundary.
  * 38 of the 123 ticket ids in simple-dispatcher's 60-day window also land in LinearViewer.
* **Survey correction on the cross-repo seam.** The 429 back-off is pinned in the shared contract: 11 `exchange` rows plus 3 `forward` rows, the 60 s cap and the 2-retry limit included. The `[done]` PR choice is pinned too: 7 `report` rows plus 7 `sentinel` rows. The two copies are byte-identical (`602ab014…`) and pinned in both suites.
  * **Genuinely unpinned:**
    * (a) The proxy limiter's 60 s window against the clients' 60 s cap. Run 10 already filed this in `docs/areas/agent-api.md`; it is still true and unchanged.
    * (b) **New, Low:** the leftover step (LIN-4373) resumes a build's own COMPLETED session, but every contract follow-up row is under a halt mode. No row pins a no-halt follow-up to a finished session.
  * The leftover wording is relayed, not parsed, so it is not a behavioural seam.
* **Routing.** The runner-contract seam is already filed in both repos: LinearViewer `agent-api.md` Waiting, plus simple-dispatcher `launch-and-harnesses.md` Lesson and Waiting. Add no mirror. Only (b) would be a new entry, in LinearViewer `runs-and-dispatch.md`, and that note is at 6142 B, so it must be pruned or distilled first.
* **Owner tickets are unchanged from mint.** LIN-4028 is In Progress; LIN-3738, 3923, 4318, 4193, 4258 and 4259 are Backlog.

**Classes** (bounds and members are in the comment, §6):

* the 38 LinearViewer production files changed since run 10, by area;
* the 4 simple-dispatcher code files changed, plus 16 unmapped;
* the 13 LinearViewer knot pairs;
* the 6 simple-dispatcher reciprocal pairs;
* the 19 LinearViewer co-change pairs with no import link;
* the contract surface: 66 rows in 12 areas, and 7 simple-dispatcher endpoints, all covered except `/api/proxy/me`;
* 3 cross-repo behaviours outside the contract;
* 2 notes at or near the cap;
* 5 sibling reports;
* 7 owner tickets.

**Recommended approach for execution**

1. Headline LinearViewer as "unchanged since run 10". Frame each ledger row against run 10's §10, keep the stable names, and report post-run-10 moves first. Give the whole-window figures from `aec9e16be` once, as baseline context.
2. Write simple-dispatcher as a baseline from three repeatable readings:
   * the require-graph reader, ported to `.mjs` and kept in the evidence folder like run 10's `edge-dump.mjs`;
   * `cochange.mjs` with simple-dispatcher's registry;
   * the shared-ticket-id count.

   Report `scope.files: 0` against 52 as could-not-read. Propose the tool gap and `shutdown.js`'s placement in the report only.
3. For the cross-repo seam, correct the survey (the 429 and `[done]` behaviour is pinned), carry the limiter↔cap entry as unchanged, and verify (b) before ranking or filing it.
4. Notes: re-verify the existing seam entries in both repos. Prune or distil `runs-and-dispatch.md` only if (b) is filed, and keep every builder Lesson. A simple-dispatcher PR is needed only if its notes change; none is required by these findings.
5. Keep the evidence folder to tool outputs and the reader script, then run the Tier-2 cold read with both clones.

Surface Assessment: \[lands cleanly\]: review-only, with no second representation, since the seam is already filed and gets no mirror.

## Implementation Plan

**Plan status:** first plan (no Plan Review Verdict in the comments). Re-grounded 10 Nov: `origin/main` is still `b315e0e8f` (LinearViewer) and `5d8489e` (simple-dispatcher); no commit in either since the ticket was created, so the ticket's references hold at HEAD.

### What this is for, and what done looks like

The operator wants a coherence baseline of the seams between areas for the 7–9 Nov window (round 1 of LIN-4344), in both repos: LinearViewer as a delta against run 10, simple-dispatcher as a first baseline with nothing to compare. It is review-only. The As-asked block's own words are the Done-when, so none is written here. Done is: a severity-ranked run 11 report with its evidence folder and area-note edits, merged by docs-only PRs; a Tier-1 or Tier-2 cold second-read recorded in one comment and in the report; a closing summary comment; LIN-4402 moved to Done.

**Cuts to the As-asked block: none.** Every clause is delivered, and the clauses the research changed are changed in the ask's favour: the survey's "429 and `[done]` are unpinned" was wrong, so the report says they are pinned. The ticket has not drifted from its purpose.

### The findings the report starts from

Research (comment of 10 Nov 07:58, "Research: LIN-4402") is the source for the measurements. I re-checked what bears on the open decisions against source at `b315e0e8f`: the contract file is `lib/runner-kit/contract.json`, 66 rows (as the research says); and its follow-up rows use only session values `live` and `none`, all but one under a halt mode (see candidate (b)). The builder re-runs every tool command itself; it does not copy numbers from the research or this plan into the report. The figures below are the ones to expect, so a mismatch is a signal to stop and look.

* LinearViewer is unchanged in structure since run 10: 13 reciprocal pairs, one nine-area cycle, no knot new or resolved. Moves: LLM⇄Runs 31/49 to 32/50; Auth⇄LLM 6/4 to 5/3; Web→Auth 69 to 67; Agent API→Runs 45 to 44. `recommendation-look-first.js` opens no notes or Periodicals edge; LIN-4393 shrank `workspace-preferences.js` by two crossings. Headline: "unchanged".
* Tool and registry are unchanged since `bad9d719` (empty `git log` on `scripts/code-shape/` and `docs/areas/areas.json`), so a delta is code movement. The window-start registry lived at `scripts/code-shape/areas.json`; the report records once that it gives identical links to the HEAD registry.
* Co-change, 60 days, HEAD registry: 929/413/76 to 942/418/76; unmapped 7216 to 8061 (documentation and evidence volume, not coupling); not shallow; the same 19 pairs lack import links.
* simple-dispatcher baseline: the standard seams tool reads 0 of 52 root CommonJS files (reported as a could-not-read count). Co-change 104/50/15 with 243 unmapped. A literal-`require` reader reads 52 files, 20 directed links, 6 reciprocal pairs (Launch⇄Reapers 2/5, Loop⇄Reapers 7/3, Launch⇄Loop 1/6, Reapers⇄Stop hook 6/2, Reapers⇄State 14/1, State⇄Stop hook 1/10).

### Which way it goes, and why

1. **Measure first, read second.** Run both tools at the three LinearViewer commits (`aec9e16be`, `bad9d719`, `b315e0e8f`) with the one HEAD registry, and co-change in both repos, before opening run 10's prose. Reason: the contract says not to re-derive numbers by search, and run 10's JSON is the yardstick. Use a detached worktree at each commit and check `git rev-parse` first: the local LinearViewer clone at `~/development/harbour/LinearViewer` is not at `b315e0e8f` (its HEAD is `732cc8e3d`), so running there would measure the wrong tree. Set aside: running the tool in the clone as it stands (wrong commit).
2. **simple-dispatcher's reader lives in the evidence folder, not the tool directory.** Port the spike to a `.mjs` reader beside run 10's `edge-dump.mjs`, with its outputs, so run 12 repeats it from the folder. The standard tool's zero-scope output sits next to it. Reason: the ask forbids editing `scripts/code-shape/`, and a method written only in prose is a weak yardstick. Set aside: patching `seams.mjs` for CommonJS (forbidden; it is a proposal in the report).
3. **Report order.** LinearViewer changes since run 10 first, then whole-window figures from `aec9e16be` once as baseline context, then the simple-dispatcher baseline, then the cross-repo seams, then proposals recorded apart from code movement, then the trend ledger. The ledger keeps run 10's stable names, marks simple-dispatcher rows baseline, and says in a line that run 10's `knot:agents-chat<->runs` is the registry's LLM & prompts ⇄ Runs & dispatch (retire or rename explicitly, one line). The report states that seams, and the cross-repo seam above all, have no full home in the notes yet.
4. **The cross-repo seam is filed once, not mirrored.** Already filed: LinearViewer `agent-api.md` Waiting (limiter window versus client cap) and simple-dispatcher `launch-and-harnesses.md` (exchange/forward Lesson, witness-case Waiting). The report states the facts: the two contract copies are identical at SHA-256 `602ab014…` and pinned by both suites; the 429 back-off (exchange and forward rows) and the `[done]` PR choice (report and sentinel rows) are pinned; leftover wording is relayed, not parsed; `/api/proxy/me` has no contract area (minor).
5. **Candidate (b), the resume-coverage gap.** The contract has no row for a follow-up, under no halt, to a finished (COMPLETED) session, which is what the leftover step (LIN-4373) does. I confirmed at the row level that the follow-up rows use `live` or `none` only, and the one no-halt follow-up row is the missing-repo case with a `live` session. Before ranking it, the builder reads the contract's `note` and what `live` means in `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs` and simple-dispatcher's `resumeSession` (`dispatcher.js`, which refuses a CANCELLED record), to be sure a COMPLETED session is not already counted as `live`. If it is not covered: Low, filed as a Waiting entry in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` citing `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` first. If it is covered: it is not a finding, and the note stays untouched. Rank it Low either way (missing coverage, no breakage observed).
6. **Notes.** Only `runs-and-dispatch.md` is expected to change, and only if (b) holds. It is 6142 of 6144 bytes, so the entry needs space from distilling: shorten wording in the longer Waiting entries (the claim-with-no-row entry is the longest) and keep every Lesson and every entry's first-cited file. The builder checks each entry it shortens is still true at HEAD rather than deleting for room. `llm-and-prompts.md` (6073 B) is touched only if a finding needs it.
